A prior benign prostate biopsy may be independently associated with more favorable surgical and biochemical outcomes after radical perineal prostatectomy. However, this association is not necessarily a predictor of the outcome in all cases. Additional studies are needed to confirm these findings.

In other words, having a prior benign prostate biopsy does not guarantee that a patient will have a better outcome after undergoing a radical perineal prostatectomy. The biopsy may have provided valuable information about the patient's overall health and cancer type, but it is just one factor among many that determine the success of the surgery.
